'''Anna Zakrisson''' (born 31 March 1980){{R|cyano}} is a Swedish [[Science communication|science communicator]] and scientist living in Berlin.

== Life ==
Born in [[Sollentuna Municipality|Sollentuna]], Stockholm, Sweden, Zakrisson grew up in Stockholm; her father was a [[hydrologist]] and her mother is a medical doctor.{{R|Merkelbach2018}} She moved to [[Fagersta Municipality]] in [[Västmanland County]] in 1988 and left Sweden in 1997 for journeys to California, Asia and Africa. She studied at [[Lucy Cavendish College, Cambridge]] and [[Stockholm University]] where she completed her doctoral thesis in 2015 entitled ''"External Growth Control of Baltic Sea Cyanobacteria"''.{{R|LCC}} From 2004 to 2006 she worked as a researcher for Max-Planck-Institute [[Cologne]].{{R|ORCiD}} She is the mother of a daughter, born 2008.{{R|Buchele}} In 2012, she moved to Berlin and worked as a biologist{{R|Friese}} and for [[Charité]].{{R|cyano|SundayLies}}

In an interview with Annika Merkelbach for [[Skeptical Inquirer]], when asked her academic career Zakrisson replied that "...I didn't want to stay in academia... The system sucks.  I think it's built to remove all that wonder and childish enthusiasm that, in my opinion, should be the foundation of science."{{R|Merkelbach2018}}

As of 2018, she is a resident of [[Berlin]], Germany, and worked as a [[freelancer]] in [[science communication]] for a two years before founding her consulting company Anna's Imaginarium GmbH & Co KG.

In 2019 Zakrisson married internationally active opera singer [[Joa Helgesson]] with whom she collaborates closely to create performative science lectures.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://hacking-health.org/hackathon2018/|title=Hackathon|first=Hacking Health|last=Berlin|date=August 2018 }}</ref>

== Science communication ==
Zakrisson was Head of Content of ''[[Zageno]]'' and worked as a biotechnical consultant there.{{R|ZagenoProfile}} She founded her platform ''Doctor Anna's Imaginarium'' in 2015.{{R|LinkedIn|Fur}} Zakrisson told Annika Merkelbach that "my absolutely favorite audience are those ... with no background whatsoever in science. To see those faces light up in sudden understanding of some aspects of their bodies or the world around them is fantastic and rewarding beyond belief."{{R|Merkelbach2018}} She also does science performances together with artists including opera singers, fakirs and dancers.{{R|Merkelbach2018}}

One of Zakrisson's main area of concern in science communication is addressing the [[Anti-vaccine activism|anti-vaccine movement]]. She calls it "an extremely dangerous movement."{{R|Merkelbach2018}}

She has become more concerned with [[Homeopathy]] since  homeopathic remedies for [[Ebola]] and HIV were introduced.{{R|Merkelbach2018}}

On the subject of women in science, Zakrisson believes that "it's important for young female scientists to be able to see the diversity of women who do science."{{R|Merkelbach2018}}

Zakrisson has cooperated with a [[Shit Museum|museum]] in the United Kingdom to advocate for early diagnostics for conditions such as [[Colorectal cancer]].{{R|Cane}}

She was a speaker at the German [[GWUP]] conference ''SkepKon'' in 2018.{{R|Harder|Merkelbach2018}} She is also active in the skeptical movement and is a member of the Swedish Skeptics Society ([[Föreningen Vetenskap och Folkbildning]]).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://skepticalinquirer.org/exclusive/on-countering-pseudoscience-educating-about-vaccinations-and-intereuropean_/|title=On Countering Pseudoscience, Educating about Vaccinations, and Intereuropean science Communication &#124; Skeptical Inquirer|first=Marc|last=Kreidler|date=17 July 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vof.se/|title=Vetenskap och Folkbildning|website=Vetenskap och Folkbildning}}</ref>

== Publications ==
* ''Control of Sodium Transport in Durum Wheat'' as Anna Zakrisson-Plogander. ASPB, March 2005. Plantphysiology, with Romola Davenport, Richard A. James, Mark Tester and Rana Munns.
* ''Do Baltic Sea diazotrophic cyanobacteria take up combined nitrogen in situ?''. Journal of Plankton Research, Volume 36, Issue 5, 1 September 2014, pp.&nbsp;1368–1380. Journal of Plankton Research, with Ulf Larsson and Helena Höglander.
* ''Regulation of heterocyst frequency in Baltic Sea Aphanizomenon sp.''. Journal of Plankton Research, Volume 36, Issue 5, 1 September 2014, pp.&nbsp;1357–1367. Journal of Plankton Research, with Ulf Larsson.
* ''External Growth Control of Baltic Sea Cyanobacteria''. Doctoral thesis, 2015. Stockholm University, Faculty of Science, Department of Ecology, Environment and Plant Sciences. [http://su.diva-portal.org/smash/record.jsf?pid=diva2%3A782894&dswid=-4113 Stockholms Universitet]
* ''Dietary supplements: health from the ocean?''. Acta Physiologica 2015, 215, pp.&nbsp;119–122. Online Library, with P. B. Persson.
* ''Did you know that your cravings might be microbes controlling your mind?''. Acta Physiologica 2015, 215, pp.&nbsp;165–166. [https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/apha.12593 Online Library]
* ''Stress''. Acta Physiologica 2016, 216, pp.&nbsp;149–152. Online Library, with P. B. Persson.
* ''Tools in science''. Acta Physiologica 2017, 220, pp.&nbsp;3–6. Online Library, with C. Kronfoth.
* ''Preservation and Fixation Methods for Aquatic Organisms''. Eureka Methods 1(1): e05. (2017) Eureka Methods with Rex J.
